thesis: The export is a plausible, low-complexity public artifact because Hugging Face supports public dataset repositories with cards and file history, but the thesis that it is a verified public artifact is not yet supported because no page read shows the live dataset, its file list, or matching checksums.

risks: The pages do not show that the named dataset exists, so its contents and checksums remain unverified.
Community-provided datasets in older documentation are flagged as unsafe by default because they can contain executable code, so users need to inspect and opt in.
If the repository were created as private instead of public, it would not be visible to anyone outside the owner or organisation members.
Large text files may not be tracked by Git LFS by default and, if greater than 10MB, may not be committed and uploaded, per the Hub upload documentation.
A dataset card that does not name every file makes read-back checks incomplete, as illustrated by the related card issue.
unknowns: Whether HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts is still shipping: None of its commits in the last 30 days is real work.

Whether hivepunk-632-4934c76e/run-record-lint-verified-fixtures-export exists as a public dataset containing README.md, fixtures.csv, fixtures.json and checksums.txt.: A read-back of the Hugging Face dataset page showing HTTP status and the four listed files.
Whether uploaded checksums match the uploaded fixture files.: checksums.txt contents and recomputed checksums for the uploaded fixtures.csv and fixtures.json from the live dataset files.

Whether the exporter has passed a standalone self-test with logged output for the version proposed for upload.: A SELFTEST_OUTPUT log or equivalent passing test output tied to the same commit or version as the four files.
Whether bee-scouts is still shipping real work.: None of its commits in the last 30 days is real work.
wouldChangeMind: A live public dataset page listing exactly the four files with matching checksums would change the thesis to verified public artifact.
A logged standalone passing self-test for the same export version would remove the main pending-verification concern.
Evidence of real, non-trivial recent commits in the underlying repo would change the assessment of ongoing shipping activity.
